kept.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
kept.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley, and vendors are prohibited from selling or providing such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.

coverage.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

kept.exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending terms, products used to set rent/income limits under affordable housing guidelines, and data used strictly for financing research, appraisals, or software development and testing.
kept.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

kept.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
kept.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or provide coordinated pricing algorithms to landlords, or for landlords to use such algorithms to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

kept.exemptions: Does not apply to aggregated and anonymous reports, products establishing rent or income limits for affordable housing guidelines, market research for financing, appraisals, or software research, testing, or training.
kept.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

kept.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
kept.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from inquiring about, requiring disclosure of, or considering criminal history during advertising, application, tenant selection, or decision-making, and cannot charge higher rent or security deposits based on criminal history.

coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley, exempting owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units and specified limited exceptions.
coverage.owner_condition: Owner-occupied properties of 1 to 3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as their primary residence.

kept.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; units under agreements allowing owner move-in under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
kept.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

kept.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
kept.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from asking about, advertising, or using criminal history in rental housing applications, tenant selection, or decision-making, with certain specific exemptions.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental housing in Berkeley with specific exemptions for lifetime sex offenders, certain public housing/Section 8 properties, and owner-occupied properties with 1 to 3 units.
coverage.owner_condition: Owner-occupied properties between 1-3 units in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence.

kept.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders, public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions, owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units), units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9, and units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
kept.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

kept.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Application Fees for Existing Tenancies
kept.requirement: Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, or to add, replace, or remove a roommate.

coverage.summary: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley.

kept.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

kept.title: Tenant Screening Fee Disclosure Requirement
kept.requirement: When charging a screening fee, landlords must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and state the maximum fee cap permitted under state law.

coverage.summary: Residential rental properties in Berkeley where a screening fee is charged.

kept.quoted_span:
When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)

kept.title: California Tenant Screening Fee Limits and Requirements
kept.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord can charge a prospective tenant is capped at $68.96 for 2026, and landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available.

coverage.summary: Prospective tenants applying for residential rental units in California.

kept.quoted_span:

$68.96

kept.title: Tenant Screening Fee Limit
kept.requirement: Landlords are subject to maximum limits on tenant screening fees and must provide a copy of the credit report, a receipt, an itemized list of expenses, and a refund of any unused portion.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties involving existing tenancies in Berkeley.

kept.title: Minimum Rental Debt Threshold for Nonpayment Eviction
kept.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent unless the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit size in the Oakland-Fremont metro area.

coverage.summary: Applies to fully or partially covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

kept.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

kept.title: Elimination of Fixed-Term Lease Renewal Refusal Eviction
kept.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from evicting a tenant solely for failing or refusing to sign a substantially similar lease upon the expiration of a fixed-term lease.

coverage.summary: Applies to fully or partially covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

kept.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

kept.title: Annual General Adjustment Maximum Cap
kept.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for fully covered rental units is capped at a maximum of 5% per year, regardless of higher Consumer Price Index calculation formulas.

coverage.summary: Applies to fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

kept.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

kept.title: Annual General Adjustment Cap
kept.requirement: The maximum Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for rent increases is capped at 5%, meaning if the rent ordinance formula produces an AGA greater than 5%, the Board-approved AGA cannot exceed 5%.

coverage.summary: Applies to fully-covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

kept.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

kept.title: Security Deposit Limit
kept.requirement: Landlords may only charge up to one month's rent as a security deposit for both unfurnished and furnished units.

coverage.summary: Most residential rental units, with exemptions for certain small landlords.
coverage.owner_condition: Exempts landlords who own no more than two rental properties with a total of no more than four residential units.

kept.title: Pre-Tenancy Unit Photograph Requirement
kept.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, landlords must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document its condition.

coverage.summary: Tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
coverage.unresolvable: Tenancy start date on or after July 1, 2025

kept.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

kept.title: Move-Out Walk-Through Inspection
kept.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify items needing repair or cleaning, giving tenants a chance to correct issues before deductions are made.

coverage.summary: All residential tenancies.

kept.quoted_span: Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning. This is to give tenants a chance to correct issues in order to avoid security deposit deductions.

kept.title: Allowed Security Deposit Deductions
kept.requirement: Landlords may only deduct from a security deposit amounts reasonably necessary to cover rent default, repair tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, clean the unit to its pre-tenancy level, or restore/replace personal property if allowed by the lease.

coverage.summary: All residential tenancies.

kept.quoted_span:
A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to:
Cover rent default
Repair damages caused by a tenant or a tenant's guest other than normal wear and tear
Clean the unit to return it to the same level of cleanliness as at the start of the tenancy (for tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003)

kept.title: Professional Cleaning Deductions Restriction
kept.requirement: Landlords cannot charge tenants or deduct from security deposits for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services unless it is reasonably necessary to return the unit to its pre-tenancy condition, minus ordinary wear and tear.

coverage.summary: All residential tenancies.

kept.quoted_span: The landlord cannot require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security deposit for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services, unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition it was in at the start of the tenancy, minus ordinary wear and tear.

kept.title: Security Deposit Return Timeline and Itemization
kept.requirement: Landlords must return the security deposit within 21 days after the tenant vacates, providing an itemized written statement and supporting documents for any deductions, including proof of completed repairs starting January 1, 2025.

coverage.summary: All residential tenancies.

kept.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant. If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions.

kept.title: Post-Possession Photograph Requirement for Deductions
kept.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of the unit after regaining possession but before making repairs or cleaning for which they intend to deduct from the security deposit, and provide these photos to the tenant.

coverage.summary: All residential tenancies where landlords intend to make security deposit deductions for repairs or cleaning.

kept.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit. These photos and a written explanation of the cost of the repairs/cleaning must be given to the tenant along with the itemized statement.

kept.title: Security Deposit Interest
kept.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

kept.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination
kept.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months (or 24 months if an adult tenant is added before 24 months). Just cause is categorized into at-fault and no-fault reasons, and no-fault evictions require relocation assistance or a final month rent waiver equal to one month's rent.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential real property after 12 or 24 months of continuous occupancy, excluding hotels, institutional housing, certain owner-occupied properties, housing less than 15 years old, separately alienable properties under specific non-corporate ownership, and deed-restricted affordable housing.

kept.exemptions: Transient occupancy, nonprofit/religious/extended care/residential care facilities, dormitories, shared bathroom/kitchen with owner, certain single-family owner-occupied residences (including ADUs/JADUs or mobilehomes), owner-occupied two-unit structures, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties (not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member) with proper notice, and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
kept.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

kept.title: N.J. Stat. § 2A:18-61.1h. Reimbursement to displaced tenant
kept.requirement: If a residential tenant is displaced because of an illegal occupancy and the municipality has not enacted a relocation ordinance, the tenant is entitled to relocation expense reimbursement from the owner equal to six times the monthly rental paid.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential tenants displaced because of an illegal occupancy where the municipality has not enacted its own relocation ordinance.

kept.exemptions: Mortgagees in possession through foreclosure are excluded.
kept.quoted_span:
If a residential tenant is displaced because of an illegal occupancy in a residential rental premises
        pursuant to paragraph (3) of subsection g. of section 2 of P.L.1974, c.49 (C.2A:18-61.1) and the
        municipality in which the rental premises is located has not enacted an ordinance pursuant to section 3 of
        P.L.1993, c.342 (C.2A:18-61.1g), the displaced residential tenant shall be entitled to reimbursement for
        relocation expenses from the owner in an amount equal to six times the monthly rental paid by the
        displaced person.

kept.title: N.J. Stat. § 2A:18-61.2. Required notice for removal
kept.requirement: Landlords seeking to remove residential tenants for good cause must provide written demand and notice for delivery of possession prior to instituting an action, with notice periods varying from 3 days to 3 years depending on the specific ground for eviction.

coverage.summary: Applies to premises covered by the Good Cause Eviction law.

kept.exemptions: Does not apply to actions for nonpayment of rent under subsection a. or f. of section 2.
kept.quoted_span:
No judgment of possession shall be entered for any premises covered by section 2 [C.2A:18-61.1] of this
      act, except in the nonpayment of rent under subsection a. or f. of section 2, unless the landlord has made
      written demand and given written notice for delivery of possession of the premises.

kept.title: N.J. Stat. § 2A:18-61.4. Waiver of rights in lease
kept.requirement: Any lease provision whereby a tenant agrees to termination or nonrenewal for other than good cause, or waives any other rights under the Act, is deemed against public policy and unenforceable.

coverage.summary: Applies to any tenant covered by section 2 of the Act.

kept.quoted_span:
Any provision in a lease whereby any tenant covered by section 2 of this act agrees that his tenancy may
         be terminated or not renewed for other than good cause as defined in section 2, or whereby the tenant
         waives any other rights under this act shall be deemed against public policy and unenforceable.

kept.title: Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant’s Source of Income
kept.requirement: Landlords cannot discriminate against tenants or prospective tenants based on their source of income, including rental assistance from government or nonprofit programs.

coverage.summary: All rental units in San Diego, except for owner-occupied units where the owner or family member shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant.
coverage.owner_condition: Owner or family member resides in the same building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant.

kept.exemptions: Tenancies in which the owner or any member of his or her family resides within the same residential building as the tenant and the owner or family member share a bathroom or a kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant.
kept.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any person to do any of the following acts, wholly or in
                           part, based on a person’s source of income (except as may be necessary to
                           comply with any program requirements related to source of income):

                           1.     To refuse to enter into or renew an agreement for tenancy;

                           2.     To interrupt or terminate any tenancy;

                           3.     To falsely represent that a rental-unit is not available for tenancy;

                           4.     To require inclusion in the terms of an agreement for tenancy any
                                  clause, condition, or restriction; or

                           5.     To restrict a tenant’s access to facilities or services on real property
                                  associated with the tenancy, or refuse repairs or improvements to real
                                  property associated with the tenancy.
